html:
Wesleyan Methodist missionaries settled in Tonga from 1826 and won over the rising chief Tāufaʻāhau, the future George Tupou I. His conversion made Methodism the leading faith of Tonga.

The church became closely tied to the crown. In 1885 the king broke with the Australian Methodist mission and set up a Free Church of Tonga, a split that caused violence and still shows in several Methodist bodies.

The Free Wesleyan Church remains the largest in Tonga and the church of the royal family. Sunday rest is written into the constitution. Missionaries also set up schools and printed the Tongan Bible, shaping the written language.
